systemUpdate.title: System update is recommended
systemUpdate.message: It seems like you're running versions of Mavlink2Rest (BlueOS) and/or ArduPilot that do not support the extended MAVLink MANUAL_CONTROL message. We strongly suggest upgrading both so you can have support for additional buttons and axes on the joystick. This is especially important if you sometimes use other control station software, like QGroundControl, as Cockpit can preferentially use the extended buttons to reduce configuration clashes. We recommend using BlueOS >= 1.2.0, and >= version 4.1.2 for ArduPilot-based autopilot firmware.

webrtcProtocols.info2: UDP can be lower latency but may drop frames, while TCP enforces frame ordering at the cost of some increased latency and jitter.

jitterBuffer.title: RTP Jitter Buffer (Target) duration:

libraryOptions.title: Video library options:
libraryOptions.info1: Configure live video processing to process videos in real-time during recording for instant availability when recording stops. This is only available in the Electron (desktop) version.
libraryOptions.info2: Choose whether to save backup raw chunks alongside the final video file. This provides safety for video reconstruction if something goes wrong, but uses approximately double the storage space.
libraryOptions.info3: Select whether video and subtitle files should be bundled together in a ZIP archive, or downloaded individually. Zipping allows a single download of a group of files, but requires waiting for the files to get zipped together. Depending on file sizes, the zipping process may complete within seconds or could take minutes.
libraryOptions.browserNoticeText: Video processing is not available in the browser version. Your recordings will be saved as raw chunks that can be downloaded and processed using the standalone version of Cockpit.
libraryOptions.liveProcessingTooltip: Process videos in real-time during recording for instant availability when recording stops
libraryOptions.liveProcessingDisabled: Live video processing is only available in the standalone version
libraryOptions.backupChunksTooltip1: Save the raw video chunks alongside the final video file for backup purposes.
libraryOptions.backupChunksTooltip2: Enabled: Raw chunks are preserved after recording. Videos use ~2x storage space but provide safety for reconstruction if the final video is corrupted.
libraryOptions.backupChunksTooltip3: Disabled: Raw chunks are automatically deleted after successful processing, using minimal storage space.
libraryOptions.backupChunksTooltip4: You can always manually clean up backup chunks later using the "Temporary" tab in the Video Library.
libraryOptions.backupChunksTooltip5: For the browser version the chunks are always saved by default.

missionEstimates.aboutText1: The values presented in this panel are analytical estimates derived from mission geometry, vehicle configuration, and manufacturer-provided nominal power curves.
missionEstimates.aboutText2: Environmental variables such as wind, current, waves, payload distribution, battery aging, and control loop behavior are not fully modeled and may introduce significant deviations from real-world performance.

tutorial.welcomeContent: Thank you for trying our control station software - we hope you make it your own!
tutorial.welcomeOpposite: This guide will assist you in connecting to your vehicle, and walk you through the available menu pages.
tutorial.mainMenuContent: Cockpit's configuration options and tools are accessed through its sidebar.
tutorial.mainMenuOpposite: Open it by clicking the highlighted tab on the left side of the screen.
tutorial.connectionsOpposite: The 'Settings' menu allows configuring Cockpit's connections and behavior.
tutorial.generalConfigContent: The 'General' page allows switching the active user, and the vehicle connection settings.
tutorial.generalConfigOpposite: Each user can have their own settings, interface profiles, and joystick mappings, which can be stored on and synchronized through the connected vehicle.
tutorial.vehicleAddressContent: Cockpit connects to a vehicle's network using a global address.
tutorial.vehicleAddressOpposite: This is usually found automatically, but if necessary you can specify a custom domain to connect to and search for the relevant vehicle components.
tutorial.interfaceConfigOpposite: Here, you'll find options to control the interface style, move the sidebar access point, and switch the display units between imperial and metric, for widgets that support it.
tutorial.joystickConfigContent: Connect a controller and move a joystick or press a button to see the current function mapping.
tutorial.joystickConfigOpposite: Fully supported joysticks have a visual configuration interface available, but there's also a mapping table provided for custom or uncommon controllers. Actions can be related to vehicle functions, can influence the display, or can run custom requests or code.
tutorial.videoConfigContent: Video sources (from MAVLink Camera Manager / BlueOS) can be given custom names, and you can configure Cockpit's receiver settings to improve performance.
tutorial.videoConfigOpposite: There are also preferences for the video recording library, to automatically process recorded chunks into video files, and zip together files when downloading multiple videos or a video with telemetry subtitles.
tutorial.telemetryRecordingOpposite: Subtitle overlays of telemetry data can be recorded with videos. This panel allows choosing which variables to include, where they appear on the screen, how the subtitles are styled, and the update rate.
tutorial.alertsConfigOpposite: Voice alerts can announce notifications and issues during operation, without covering the screen. The voice and reported alert severities can be configured here.
tutorial.devSettingsContent: This section includes settings and Cockpit logs to help with development and advanced troubleshooting.
tutorial.devSettingsOpposite: We recommend leaving the default values, but if you prefer to you can stop Cockpit from synchronizing its settings with BlueOS vehicles, and/or disable sending the anonymous usage statistics and error messages that help the development team to find performance issues and bugs.
tutorial.missionConfigOpposite: This panel allows selecting which vehicle commands require an extra confirmation step before sending, to avoid triggering mission- or safety-critical functions accidentally.
tutorial.completedOpposite: If you want to see it again, this guide can be reopened through 'Settings' > 'General'. For further support, please reach out through the channels listed in the 'About' section of the sidebar.
tutorial.reopenMessage: This guide can be reopened via the Settings > General menu

wizard.ignoreExplanation: You will keep your current views group and joystick mapping for {vehicle}. This walkthrough will not open automatically again for this vehicle.
wizard.safety: A correct joystick mapping is important: a mismatched mapping can cause motors to spin unexpectedly as soon as the vehicle is armed.
wizard.laterViews: Default views: open the Edit menu and choose Import vehicle defaults.
wizard.laterJoystick: Default joystick mapping: open Joystick configuration and use the import button on the mapping toolbar.
wizard.finished: You have finished reviewing the default configuration for {vehicle}. This dialog will not open automatically again for this vehicle.
wizard.laterInstructions: To import defaults later, use Import vehicle defaults in the Edit menu, or the import button in Joystick configuration.
wizard.viewsIntro: NaviLync includes the following default views for {vehicle}. Select views, choose how to apply them, and check the preview.
wizard.viewsMatch: Your views group already includes the defaults for {vehicle}. Click Next to finish.
wizard.noViewsDefault: No default views are available for {vehicle}.
wizard.introNext: Click Next to review the defaults and decide whether to import them.
wizard.introDetection: NaviLync detected a non-default configuration for {vehicle}. Import defaults or keep your current setup.
wizard.introOptions: Review the joystick mapping and views on the next screens. Append or replace views, and select joystick bindings to import.
wizard.introOnce: This walkthrough opens automatically once per vehicle. Defaults remain available in the Edit menu and Joystick configuration.
wizard.introIgnore: Click Ignore to keep your current views group and joystick mapping.
